meta.name: English
meta.greeting: Hello. Send me a bank message and I will tell you if it is real.

ui.choose_hint: Tap to hear it. Pick the one that sounds like home.
ui.sender_hint: e.g. JD-SBIINB-S or a phone number
ui.clicked_btn: Already clicked a link or shared OTP?
ui.thanks: Thanks. We will look at it.
ui.cif_prompt: Your CIF / customer number (it is in your passbook)
ui.not_verified_note: We have not yet confirmed this step on the bank's website. Check once at the branch.
ui.footer: Vaani never asks for your OTP, PIN or password.
ui.ask_hint: e.g. What is CIF? Which papers do I need?
ui.ask_fallback: I am not sure about that. Please ask at your bank branch or call {helpline}.

real.headline: Looks real
real.say: This message looks like it really came from {bank}.

fake.headline: Fake
fake.say: This message is fake. Do not open the link and do not tell anyone your OTP or PIN.

not_sure.headline: Not sure
not_sure.say: I cannot confirm this message. Do not click anything. Call your bank on the number printed on your card or passbook.

reasons.asks_secret: It asks for your OTP, PIN or password. A bank never asks for these.
reasons.remote_app: It asks you to install a screen-sharing app like AnyDesk. That lets a stranger control your phone.
reasons.apk_file: The link downloads an app file (.apk). Banks do not send apps by SMS.
reasons.lookalike_link: The link {link} copies the name of {imitates}, but it is not their website.
reasons.link_not_official: The link {link} is not on {bank}'s list of official websites.
reasons.link_other_bank: The link belongs to {owner}, not the bank named in the message.
reasons.suspicious_link: The link {link} is not a bank website and uses words like '{words}'.
reasons.shortener: The link is a short link ({link}), which hides where it really goes.
reasons.personal_number_sender: It came from a normal mobile number ({sender}). Banks send alerts from a bank name like XX-SBIINB.
reasons.promo_header: It came as a promotion message, not a bank service alert.
reasons.sender_other_bank: The sender belongs to {owner}, not the bank named in the message.
reasons.sender_unknown: We do not know this sender name ({sender}).
reasons.call_mobile_number: It asks you to call a mobile number ({numbers}). Banks give toll-free numbers.
reasons.urgency: It tries to scare you into hurrying ('{matched}').
reasons.reward_bait: It promises a prize, refund or cashback to make you click.
reasons.link_official: The link goes to {bank}'s official website.
reasons.sender_known: The sender name is one {bank} uses.
reasons.clean: No red flags. It reads like a normal {bank} alert and has no link.
reasons.no_bank: The message does not name a bank we know.
reasons.link_from_voice: You read the link aloud. I can only check a link exactly when you paste it or send a photo.
reasons.asks_secret_llm: It asks for your OTP, PIN or password. A bank never asks for these.
reasons.model_scam: Our scam-SMS model, trained on thousands of real scam and normal messages, says this one reads like a scam.

fake: Do not reply and do not call any number in the message.
If you want, report it on 1930 or sancharsaathi.gov.in.
not_sure: Ask them if this message is from them.
rekyc: Your bank wants your ID papers again (this is called re-KYC).
Keep your Aadhaar and PAN ready.
rekyc_branch_only: Go to your home branch with Aadhaar and PAN.
Nobody from the bank will ask for OTP for this.
mandate_fail: An automatic payment (auto-debit) from your account did not go through.
Keep {amount_or_enough} in the account before the next try.
If you do not know this payment, call {bank} on {helpline}.
card_blocked: Call {bank} on {helpline} or visit your branch to unblock it.
Never unblock through a link in an SMS.
payment_due: Pay through the bank's own app or at the branch, not through an SMS link.
transaction: If you did not do this, call {bank} on {helpline} right away.
otp_info: This is a one-time password for something you are doing.
If you did not ask for it, do not tell it to anyone, not even a bank caller.
generic_real: Nothing to worry about. If in doubt, ask at your branch.

channels.portal: Or fill it on the bank's own page: {url}
channels.branch: Or go to your home branch.
channels.official_app: Or do it in the official {name} app.
channels.netbanking: Or do it in the bank's own net banking.

clicked.title: Do these now, in this order
steps: Turn on flight mode now. This cuts off anyone controlling your phone.
If you installed AnyDesk or any app the caller told you to, uninstall it.
Call your bank on {helpline} and ask them to block your card, UPI and net banking.
Call 1930 (cyber crime helpline). The sooner you call, the better the chance to stop the money.
Also file a complaint on cybercrime.gov.in. Keep screenshots of the message.
Change your UPI PIN and net banking password from a safe phone.

glossary.KYC: your ID papers with the bank
glossary.OTP: the secret number the bank sends you

bits.card_number: the number printed on your card or passbook
